identity.role: Senior Software Engineer + AppSec Specialist + System Architect
rules: NO_PLACEHOLDERS: Always write complete, functional, ready-to-run code.
NO_HALLUCINATIONS: Validate schema and route definitions before generation.
AUTO_WIRING: Always register dependencies, routes, permissions, and navigation automatically.
ZERO_TRUST_SECURITY: Enforce OWASP Top 10 security guardrails at every layer of generation.
STRICT_FRAMEWORK_RULE: You are using SLIM 4, NOT LARAVEL. DO NOT USE Laravel Facades (e.g. View::, Validator::, DB::), DO NOT USE Laravel HTTP Requests (Illuminate\Http\Request) or FormRequest.
STRICT_PSR7_RULE: ALWAYS use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface and Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface for Controllers.

HOOK_PROTECTION: app/Hooks/{ModelName}Hooks.php files are created ONCE and must NEVER be overwritten, edited, or regenerated after they first exist — always check file existence before writing one. See hook_protocol and canonical_snippets.hooks_pattern.

NO_EXTERNAL_FETCH: NEVER attempt to download, curl, or fetch anything from the internet during code generation (assets, reference templates, package files). Every third-party asset or reference this project needs is already saved locally (public/assets/vendor/ for runtime assets, reference/ for design/structure references) — if something seems missing, say so instead of trying to fetch it.

CONSTRUCTOR_CALL_SITE_PAIRING: For any class instantiated manually with `new X(...)` (i.e. NOT resolved automatically via PHP-DI autowiring — this includes every Middleware attached with ->add(new X(...)) in routes/web.php), the class's __construct() and every place that calls `new X(...)` MUST come from the SAME canonical_snippets entry, copied together in the same step. NEVER write the constructor in one file from memory and the instantiation call in another file from memory — verified by real 7B testing to silently produce argument-order/type mismatches that crash at runtime (see verified_gotchas.middleware_constructor_call_site_mismatch).

onboarding_protocol.rule: When starting on a NEW or EMPTY project directory, AI MUST proactively ask the user before writing business modules:
onboarding_protocol.mandatory_question: Proyek ini masih baru/kosong. Apakah Anda ingin menginisialisasi Starter Skeleton Boilerplate (lengkap dengan Auth, Login, Profile, Base Layout, Sidebar & Navbar) terlebih dahulu, atau ingin langsung membuat modul dari proyek kosong?
options: Option A: Generate Starter Skeleton Boilerplate first (Recommended for full apps)
Option B: Build custom module directly on a clean/blank slate

hook_protocol.description: Inspired by PHPMaker's Server Events mechanism (verified by inspecting its actual generator template package): PHPMaker splices user-authored PHP, stored SEPARATELY from generated files, into fixed injection points (Page_Load, Page_DataRendering, etc.) so regenerating a page NEVER destroys custom business logic. We replicate the same base/custom separation for this framework.
hook_protocol.rule: Every {ModelName}Service.php MUST call out to a companion App\Hooks\{ModelName}Hooks.php at fixed points (see canonical_snippets.hooks_pattern). The Service class MAY be freely regenerated/rewritten on every request. The Hooks class MUST be created ONLY THE FIRST TIME a module is scaffolded — if app/Hooks/{ModelName}Hooks.php already exists, AI MUST leave it completely untouched, no matter what changes are requested to the module, unless the user EXPLICITLY asks to edit that specific hooks file.
hook_protocol.why: Without this separation, every 'regenerate this module' or 'add a field to this table' request forces the AI to rewrite the whole Service class from scratch, silently deleting any business-specific logic (discounts, stock checks, notifications, etc.) a human or a previous AI session had added inside it. Splitting fixed CRUD plumbing (regenerable) from business rules (permanent, hand-authored) mirrors exactly how PHPMaker survives re-generation without losing customization.

backend.framework: Slim Framework 4 (PSR-7/15) ONLY. Do NOT use Bramus Router or any other routing library — routes are always defined via $app->get()/post()/etc. on the Slim App instance.

libraries.select: Choices.js (trigger class: `data-choices`, NOT `select2` — do not confuse with jQuery Select2)
libraries.ui_components: Flowbite (dropdowns, modals, tooltips built on Tailwind)

design_system.description: Structural/visual reference for every Twig template. Purpose: give AI a fixed, small vocabulary of Tailwind values to reuse instead of picking new-but-similar values each time (e.g. rounded-2xl vs rounded-xl) — the same discipline canonical_snippets applies to PHP, applied here to markup.
design_system.reference_template: Flowbite Admin Dashboard, MIT license. NEVER fetch it from GitHub — a 7B model cannot reliably download external URLs at generation time. The actual source files are already saved locally at reference/flowbite-admin-dashboard/ (see its README.md for how to use them). Use its PAGE STRUCTURE and COMPONENT MECHANICS (sidebar, navbar, tables, cards, forms) as the layout reference. Do NOT copy its default gray-only color theme or dark: classes — this project uses its own brand tokens below. Prefer rules/ui_templates.md (already Twig-adapted) over the raw reference/ files whenever the pattern you need is already covered there.
design_system.sidebar_accordion_mechanism: Flowbite's native collapse component (data-collapse-toggle="{id}" on the trigger, id="{id}" + class="hidden" on the target <ul>/<div>) — NOT the native HTML5 <details>/<summary> element used in an earlier version of this spec. flowbite.min.js is already loaded on every layout so this needs zero extra JS. See rules/ui_templates.md section 3 for the literal markup.
design_system.dark_mode: NOT enabled. The reference template ships `dark:` variants on every class by default; this project deliberately omits them to keep generated markup shorter and reduce the chance a 7B model applies dark: inconsistently. Do not add dark: classes unless explicitly requested.
design_system.responsive_app_shell: MANDATORY (see verified_gotchas.app_shell_not_responsive and navbar_covered_by_mobile_sidebar). The sidebar is a mobile drawer: id="sidebar", fixed lg:static, top-16 lg:top-auto bottom-0 lg:bottom-auto (NEVER inset-y-0 — see the gotcha), -translate-x-full lg:translate-x-0, transition-transform. It is opened/closed by clicking #sidebar-toggle (a hamburger button in navbar.twig, lg:hidden) or #sidebar-backdrop (a dark overlay in base.twig, lg:hidden), both handled by initSidebarToggle() already inside the pre-provisioned public/assets/vendor/js/app.js — do not write new JS for this, just include the three elements with those exact ids. See rules/ui_templates.md sections 1-3 for the literal markup.

canonical_snippets.description: Literal, copy-paste-ready code that MUST be reused verbatim (only rename Model/Table/fields) instead of being regenerated from scratch. These exist because a 7B-class model is prone to hallucinating APIs for standalone/niche libraries — always prefer these over inventing new code.

eloquent_capsule_bootstrap.target_path: app/bootstrap.php, required from public/index.php BEFORE the Slim App/DI container is built
eloquent_capsule_bootstrap.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Database\Capsule\Manager as Capsule;
use Illuminate\Pagination\Paginator;

$capsule = new Capsule;
$capsule->addConnection([
    'driver'    => 'mysql',
    'host'      => $_ENV['DB_HOST'],
    'database'  => $_ENV['DB_DATABASE'],
    'username'  => $_ENV['DB_USERNAME'],
    'password'  => $_ENV['DB_PASSWORD'],
    'charset'   => 'utf8mb4',
    'collation' => 'utf8mb4_unicode_ci',
    'prefix'    => '',
]);

$capsule->setAsGlobal();
$capsule->bootEloquent();

// REQUIRED for ->paginate() to work at all outside full Laravel (see
// verified_gotchas.pagination_resolvers_never_registered) — without these,
// Paginator::resolveCurrentPage() always returns 1 and resolveCurrentPath()
// always returns '/', regardless of the real request.
Paginator::currentPathResolver(function () {
    return strtok($_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] ?? '/', '?');
});
Paginator::currentPageResolver(function (string $pageName = 'page') {
    return (int) ($_GET[$pageName] ?? 1);
});
Paginator::queryStringResolver(function () {
    return $_GET;
});
eloquent_capsule_bootstrap.note: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07), root-caused by reading vendor/illuminate/pagination/AbstractPaginator.php directly: illuminate/pagination used standalone (no full Laravel framework) does NOT auto-detect the current page or request path from the HTTP request. Eloquent\Builder::paginate() DOES call Paginator::resolveCurrentPage() and Paginator::resolveCurrentPath() internally, but both silently return hardcoded defaults (page 1, path '/') unless the three resolvers above are registered ONCE at boot. Without this, EVERY paginated list is stuck on page 1 forever no matter what ?page=N is in the URL, and every pagination link points to '/' instead of the real route — this is the actual root cause behind verified_gotchas.pagination_footer_was_never_functional, deeper than the missing Twig markup that was also fixed alongside it.

composer_json_template.target_path: composer.json — created ONCE at the very start of any project (step 0, before any other boilerplate file). This is the COMPLETE, verified-working require block — copy it VERBATIM, only replacing {vendor}/{project}/{description}. Then run `composer install`.
composer_json_template.note: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): a fresh project crashed with 'Class "Illuminate\Pagination\Paginator" not found' in app/bootstrap.php because illuminate/pagination was missing from composer.json. Root cause: this package was ONLY ever mentioned as a warning in verified_gotchas (eloquent_pagination_needs_separate_package) — never as an actual literal entry in a composer.json the AI could copy verbatim, so the AI had to infer the package name from a `use Illuminate\Pagination\Paginator;` statement buried inside canonical_snippets.eloquent_capsule_bootstrap's code, and missed it. Since bootstrap.php registers Paginator resolvers on EVERY request (not just paginated list pages), illuminate/pagination is a HARD REQUIREMENT from the very first request, not an optional add-later package — this composer.json already includes it. NEVER write composer.json's require block from memory or by inferring packages from `use` statements scattered across other snippets — always copy this exact block, it is the one proven via a real `composer install` + full working app in this review.
composer_json_template.VERSION_PINS_ARE_EXACT_DO_NOT_LOOSEN: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): a separate test run ended up with odan/session 6.x installed instead of the 5.x this whole framework was built and verified against, and crashed with a fatal error because PhpSession::setOptions() was removed in 6.x (options now go through the constructor instead) — a breaking API change vs canonical_snippets.starter_middleware_pattern and app/dependencies.php, which both use the 5.x setOptions() call. Every version constraint in this composer.json (e.g. "odan/session": "^5.1") is EXACT and already tested — do NOT loosen, omit, or 'helpfully' upgrade any of them, even if a newer major version exists. If `composer install` ever resolves a different major version than what's pinned here, something has gone wrong upstream (e.g. a corrupted or hand-edited composer.json) — investigate rather than adapting the code to the newer API.

public_index_php_template.target_path: public/index.php — the single entry point for the entire app. Created ONCE, copy VERBATIM.
public_index_php_template.note: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): this exact file was NEVER given as a literal canonical_snippet before now, despite being the most foundational file in the whole app — it was only ever described in prose across three separate scattered notes (index_php_strict_rules.middleware_execution_order, verified_gotchas.twig_middleware_wiring, verified_gotchas.middleware_constructor_call_site_mismatch). A real 7B test run had to self-correct THREE separate times on this one file in sequence: (1) forgot to register TwigMiddleware at all -> 'Twig could not be found in the server request attributes', (2) added it via TwigMiddleware::createFromContainer() -> same error persists because that method never sets the attribute, (3) finally switched to TwigMiddleware::create(). All three mistakes are things this exact file already gets right — the AI just never had it as a literal artifact to copy, only assembled it from memory across disconnected notes. NEVER reconstruct public/index.php from the prose rules alone — copy this file verbatim, the prose rules exist to explain WHY it looks this way, not as a spec to re-derive it from.
public_index_php_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

use App\Middleware\CsrfViewMiddleware;
use DI\ContainerBuilder;
use Odan\Session\SessionInterface;
use Slim\Csrf\Guard;
use Slim\Factory\AppFactory;
use Slim\Views\Twig;
use Slim\Views\TwigMiddleware;

require dirname(__DIR__) . '/vendor/autoload.php';
require dirname(__DIR__) . '/app/bootstrap.php';

$containerBuilder = new ContainerBuilder();
(require dirname(__DIR__) . '/app/dependencies.php')($containerBuilder);
$container = $containerBuilder->build();

AppFactory::setContainer($container);
$app = AppFactory::create();

// index_php_strict_rules.session_handling: always start the session via the
// container-bound SessionInterface, never raw session_start().
$container->get(SessionInterface::class)->start();

(require dirname(__DIR__) . '/routes/web.php')($app);

// index_php_strict_rules.middleware_execution_order: add() in THIS exact order.
// Slim executes middleware FILO (first add() call = LAST to execute), so real
// execution order is the reverse of the add() calls below:
//   ErrorMiddleware -> BodyParsingMiddleware -> RoutingMiddleware -> TwigMiddleware
//   -> Guard -> CsrfViewMiddleware -> route handler.
// TwigMiddleware MUST execute before CsrfViewMiddleware (which calls
// Twig::fromRequest() and needs the "view" request attribute already set), so it is
// added AFTER Guard/CsrfViewMiddleware here even though Twig runs earlier than both.
// NOTE: TwigMiddleware::createFromContainer() looks up Twig via the container but
// silently NEVER sets the "view" request attribute (its $attributeName stays null
// internally) — Twig::fromRequest() then always throws. Use ::create() explicitly
// instead, passing the resolved Twig instance and the attribute name.
$app->add(CsrfViewMiddleware::class);
$app->add(Guard::class);
$app->add(TwigMiddleware::create($app, $container->get(Twig::class), 'view'));
$app->addRoutingMiddleware();
$app->addBodyParsingMiddleware();

$isLocal = ($_ENV['APP_ENV'] ?? 'production') === 'local';
$app->addErrorMiddleware($isLocal, true, true);

$app->run();

twig_custom_extensions.target_path: app/dependencies.php, registered on the Twig environment right after Twig::create()
twig_custom_extensions.note: REQUIRED because views use `|initials` filter and `can()` function — without this registration Twig throws Twig\Error\SyntaxError at runtime.

controller_twig_render.note: The ONLY correct way to render a view from a Controller. Never use Laravel's view() helper.
controller_twig_render.code:

csrf_twig_globals_middleware.target_path: app/Middleware/CsrfViewMiddleware.php, registered AFTER Slim\Csrf\Guard so csrf attributes already exist on the request. Also the correct place to persist the session (see verified_gotchas.session_never_persisted_without_save).
csrf_twig_globals_middleware.note: VERIFIED BY ACTUALLY RUNNING THE APP (2026-08-06). csrf.keys.name/csrf.keys.value are the Guard's getTokenNameKey()/getTokenValueKey() — CONSTANT strings like 'csrf_name'/'csrf_value' — NOT separate request attributes. There is no 'csrf_name_key'/'csrf_value_key' attribute; an earlier version of this spec used that and it silently rendered `name=""` on both hidden inputs, breaking every POST form.

starter_middleware_pattern.description: AuthMiddleware, RbacMiddleware, and RateLimitMiddleware were previously ONLY named as filenames in starter_boilerplate_blueprint.json with zero code — VERIFIED BY ACTUAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07, local Gemini model generating a fresh project 'wberingin') that this causes a real, reproducible crash: the model wrote RbacMiddleware's constructor with one parameter order, then instantiated it in routes/web.php with a DIFFERENT, incompatible argument order/count, because it had no fixed contract to copy from and reinvented each side independently in a different file. Exact error produced: "RbacMiddleware::__construct(): Argument #2 ($session) must be of type Odan\Session\SessionInterface, Slim\Psr7\Factory\ResponseFactory given". FIX: all three classes AND their exact instantiation call sites are given together below as ONE inseparable unit — never write the class body and its `new X(...)` call from memory in two different files; copy both from here verbatim.

auth_middleware_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Middleware;

use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\MenuBuilder;
use Odan\Session\SessionInterface;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseFactoryInterface;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface as Response;
use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface as Request;
use Psr\Http\Server\MiddlewareInterface;
use Psr\Http\Server\RequestHandlerInterface as Handler;
use Slim\Views\Twig;

class AuthMiddleware implements MiddlewareInterface
{
    private const IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly SessionInterface $session,
        private readonly ResponseFactoryInterface $responseFactory,
        private readonly MenuBuilder $menuBuilder,
    ) {
    }

    public function process(Request $request, Handler $handler): Response
    {
        if (!$this->session->has('user_id')) {
            return $this->redirect('/login');
        }

        $lastActivity = (int) ($this->session->get('last_activity') ?? time());
        if ((time() - $lastActivity) > self::IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) {
            $this->session->clear();
            $this->session->regenerateId();
            return $this->redirect('/login');
        }
        $this->session->set('last_activity', time());

        $path = $request->getUri()->getPath();
        if ($this->session->get('must_change_password') && !str_starts_with($path, '/profile/password') && !str_starts_with($path, '/logout')) {
            return $this->redirect('/profile/password');
        }

        $authUser = User::find($this->session->get('user_id'));
        $menu = $this->menuBuilder->build(dirname(__DIR__) . '/menu.php', (array) $this->session->get('permissions'));

        $view = Twig::fromRequest($request)->getEnvironment();
        $view->addGlobal('auth_user', $authUser);
        $view->addGlobal('menu', $menu);

        return $handler->handle($request);
    }

    private function redirect(string $path): Response
    {
        return $this->responseFactory->createResponse(302)->withHeader('Location', $path);
    }
}

rbac_middleware_template.note: Constructor parameter order is SessionInterface, then ResponseFactoryInterface, then string $requiredPermission — in exactly that order. This is the exact class that broke in 7B testing; do not reorder.
rbac_middleware_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Middleware;

use Odan\Session\SessionInterface;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseFactoryInterface;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface as Response;
use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface as Request;
use Psr\Http\Server\MiddlewareInterface;
use Psr\Http\Server\RequestHandlerInterface as Handler;

class RbacMiddleware implements MiddlewareInterface
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly SessionInterface $session,
        private readonly ResponseFactoryInterface $responseFactory,
        private readonly string $requiredPermission,
    ) {
    }

    public function process(Request $request, Handler $handler): Response
    {
        $permissions = (array) $this->session->get('permissions');

        if (!in_array($this->requiredPermission, $permissions, true)) {
            $response = $this->responseFactory->createResponse(403);
            $response->getBody()->write('403 Forbidden: Anda tidak memiliki akses.');
            return $response;
        }

        return $handler->handle($request);
    }
}

rate_limit_middleware_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Middleware;

use App\Models\AuditLog;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseFactoryInterface;
use Psr\Http\Message\ResponseInterface as Response;
use Psr\Http\Message\ServerRequestInterface as Request;
use Psr\Http\Server\MiddlewareInterface;
use Psr\Http\Server\RequestHandlerInterface as Handler;

class RateLimitMiddleware implements MiddlewareInterface
{
    private const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5;
    private const WINDOW_MINUTES = 15;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly ResponseFactoryInterface $responseFactory,
    ) {
    }

    public function process(Request $request, Handler $handler): Response
    {
        $ip = $this->clientIp($request);

        $attempts = AuditLog::where('action', 'login_failed')
            ->where('ip_address', $ip)
            ->where('created_at', '>=', date('Y-m-d H:i:s', time() - self::WINDOW_MINUTES * 60))
            ->count();

        if ($attempts >= self::MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
            $response = $this->responseFactory->createResponse(429);
            $response->getBody()->write('Terlalu banyak percobaan login. Coba lagi dalam beberapa menit.');
            return $response;
        }

        return $handler->handle($request);
    }

    private function clientIp(Request $request): string
    {
        $server = $request->getServerParams();
        return $server['REMOTE_ADDR'] ?? '0.0.0.0';
    }
}

route_wiring_matching_call_sites.target_path: routes/web.php — THE EXACT instantiation call for each middleware above. Argument order/count here MUST match each __construct() above exactly.

hooks_pattern.description: PHPMaker-inspired base/custom split (see hook_protocol). The Service is fully regenerable; the Hooks class is written once and permanently owned by whoever customizes it — human or a past AI session.

hooks_class_template.creation_rule: ONLY create this file if it does not already exist. If it exists, NEVER modify it as part of regenerating {ModelName}Service.php or any other step.
hooks_class_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Hooks;

use App\Models\{ModelName};

/**
 * Business-specific customization for {ModelName}. Created ONCE by the AI — never
 * regenerated or overwritten afterwards, even when {ModelName}Service.php itself
 * is rewritten. Add discounts, stock checks, notifications, cross-module side
 * effects, etc. here instead of inside the Service.
 */
class {ModelName}Hooks
{
    public function beforeCreate(array $data): array
    {
        return $data; // mutate/validate $data before insert, or throw to abort
    }

    public function afterCreate({ModelName} $model): void
    {
    }

    public function beforeUpdate({ModelName} $model, array $data): array
    {
        return $data;
    }

    public function afterUpdate({ModelName} $model): void
    {
    }

    public function beforeDelete({ModelName} $model): void
    {
        // throw to abort deletion (e.g. still referenced elsewhere)
    }

    public function afterDelete({ModelName} $model): void
    {
    }
}

service_calling_hooks_example.note: Every CUD method in the Service MUST call the matching hook at these exact points — before the write inside the transaction, and after it but still inside the transaction (so a hook exception rolls back the write too).

menu_registry_pattern.description: PHPMaker-inspired (verified by inspecting its actual menu.html template: sidebar/navbar items are built from a metadata array — id, label, url, parentId, security, icon — rendered by ONE generic mechanism, never hand-authored HTML per module). Adopting a new module's nav link must NEVER require editing sidebar.twig's HTML/accordion structure — that is the #1 way a 7B model corrupts an unrelated module's markup.

menu_php_template.target_path: app/menu.php — created once by the starter boilerplate; every later module APPENDS one array entry here, nothing else
menu_php_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * Central navigation registry. resources/views/partials/sidebar.twig renders this
 * array GENERICALLY. NEVER hand-edit sidebar.twig's HTML to add a nav link —
 * append one entry here instead.
 *
 * Fields:
 *   id         string  unique key. Also used as the 'parent' value for children.
 *   label      string  visible text.
 *   route      ?string url, or null for a parent-only accordion header with no link.
 *   icon       ?string key into the $icons map defined in sidebar.twig, or null.
 *   permission ?string permission slug required to see this item, or null = always visible.
 *   parent     ?string id of the parent item to nest under (accordion), or null = top-level.
 */
return [
    [
        'id' => 'dashboard',
        'label' => 'Dashboard',
        'route' => '/dashboard',
        'icon' => 'dashboard',
        'permission' => null,
        'parent' => null,
    ],
    // Add new modules here, e.g.:
    // [
    //     'id' => '{module}',
    //     'label' => '{Label}',
    //     'route' => '/{module}',
    //     'icon' => null,
    //     'permission' => '{module}.view',
    //     'parent' => null, // or an existing group id
    // ],
];

menu_builder_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

namespace App\Support;

class MenuBuilder
{
    /**
     * @param string[] $permissions
     * @return array<int, array<string, mixed>>
     */
    public function build(string $menuFilePath, array $permissions): array
    {
        $items = require $menuFilePath;

        $visible = array_values(array_filter(
            $items,
            static fn (array $item): bool => $item['permission'] === null || in_array($item['permission'], $permissions, true)
        ));

        $topLevel = array_values(array_filter(
            $visible,
            static fn (array $item): bool => $item['parent'] === null
        ));

        foreach ($topLevel as &$node) {
            $node['children'] = array_values(array_filter(
                $visible,
                static fn (array $item): bool => $item['parent'] === $node['id']
            ));
        }
        unset($node);

        return $topLevel;
    }
}

wiring.note: Built once per request in AuthMiddleware (already has the session and is already computing the auth_user Twig global) and exposed as the `menu` Twig global. Registered in app/dependencies.php as \App\Support\MenuBuilder::class => \DI\autowire(), and injected into AuthMiddleware's constructor wherever it is instantiated (routes/web.php).

menu_registry_pattern.sidebar_render_note: sidebar.twig loops `{% for item in menu %}`, rendering a Flowbite data-collapse-toggle accordion (see design_system.sidebar_accordion_mechanism) when `item.children` is non-empty and a plain <a> otherwise. A small `{% set icons = {...} %}` dict at the top of sidebar.twig maps icon keys to inline SVG — that dict is the ONLY part of sidebar.twig a new module may need to touch (to add a new icon key), never the loop/render logic itself.

field_schema_pattern.description: PHPMaker-inspired (verified by inspecting its field.xml settings + list-single-column.html field loop: every column/input is rendered by ONE generic mechanism driven by a small per-field metadata array — name, format/type, validation — never hand-written per field). Adopting this means a new CRUD module needs only a small data array, not hand-written <input>/<td> markup for every field. This is deliberately GENERIC — not POS-specific — because it must repeat identically across any future project built on this framework, exactly like PHPMaker's own field settings.
field_schema_pattern.field_types_fixed_vocabulary: text | textarea | number | date | select | checkbox | password — ONLY these seven. Every one already has a matching local vendor library wired in app.js (date -> Flatpickr via class datepicker, select -> Choices.js via class data-choices, the rest are plain HTML). NEVER invent a new type without updating partials/_form_field.twig first. `password` NEVER echoes the current value back into the input (see canonical_snippets.rbac_management_forms_pattern for why admin user-edit forms should avoid a password field entirely and use a separate reset action instead).

field_schema_template.target_path: app/FieldSchemas/{ModelName}FieldSchema.php — the SINGLE source of truth for this model's fields. Feeds: Rakit validation rules (step 4), list table columns AND add/edit form inputs (step 9). Created once per module; edited in place when a field is added/removed (unlike Hooks, this file IS meant to be maintained as the model evolves).
field_schema_template.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

/**
 * Field definitions for {ModelName}. Single source of truth — read by
 * {Action}{ModelName}Request (validation), and by the list/add/edit Twig views
 * via partials/_form_field.twig (rendering). Never duplicate field markup by hand
 * when this schema already describes the field.
 *
 * Fields:
 *   name    string   column/input name, matches the DB column and Eloquent $fillable entry.
 *   label   string   human label shown in <label>/<th>.
 *   type    string   one of: text | textarea | number | date | select | checkbox.
 *   rules   string   Rakit\Validation rule string, e.g. 'required|max:255' (NEVER include
 *                    'string' — Rakit has no such rule, see verified_gotchas).
 *   options ?array   [['value' => ..., 'label' => ...], ...] — REQUIRED when type = select, else null.
 *   show_in string[] subset of ['list', 'add', 'edit'] — which pages render this field.
 */
return [
    [
        'name' => 'nama',
        'label' => 'Nama',
        'type' => 'text',
        'rules' => 'required|max:255',
        'options' => null,
        'show_in' => ['list', 'add', 'edit'],
    ],
    // Add more fields here, e.g.:
    // [
    //     'name' => 'kategori_id',
    //     'label' => 'Kategori',
    //     'type' => 'select',
    //     'rules' => 'required|integer',
    //     'options' => null, // populated by the Controller at render time from the DB, see wiring note
    //     'show_in' => ['list', 'add', 'edit'],
    // ],
];

request_deriving_rules_from_schema.target_path: app/Requests/{ModelName}Request.php — ONE class shared by both Add and Edit (not two separate {Action}{ModelName}Request classes), parameterized by `$action`. REPLACES the old hardcoded-rules template in step 4. Rules now come from the schema, so validation can never drift out of sync with the form/list.
request_deriving_rules_from_schema.note: VERIFIED BY ACTUALLY IMPLEMENTING AND RUNNING A FULL CRUD MODULE (2026-08-07, Users). The rules array MUST be filtered by whether `$action` appears in each field's `show_in` — otherwise a field like `password` (show_in: ['add'] only) would still be pulled into the Edit rules and wrongly required even though the Edit form never renders it, since it silently disappears from the submitted POST body.
request_deriving_rules_from_schema.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
namespace App\Requests;

use Rakit\Validation\Validator;
use Exception;

class {ModelName}Request
{
    /**
     * @param 'add'|'edit' $action Only fields whose `show_in` contains this action
     *                             are validated.
     */
    public static function validate(array $data, string $action): array
    {
        $fields = require dirname(__DIR__) . '/FieldSchemas/{ModelName}FieldSchema.php';

        $rules = [];
        foreach ($fields as $field) {
            if (in_array($action, $field['show_in'], true)) {
                $rules[$field['name']] = $field['rules'];
            }
        }

        $validator = new Validator();
        $validation = $validator->make($data, $rules);
        $validation->validate();
        if ($validation->fails()) {
            throw new Exception($validation->errors()->all()[0]);
        }
        return $validation->getValidData();
    }
}

form_field_macro_template.target_path: resources/views/partials/_form_field.twig — created ONCE, shared by every module's add/edit view. NEVER hand-write an <input> for a field this macro already covers.

add_edit_view_usage.note: Controller passes `fields` (the schema array, options resolved for any select fields) and `data` (current values, empty for Add) to the view. See canonical_snippets.controller_twig_render for the base render pattern this extends.

list_columns_usage.note: The SAME schema drives the list table's <thead>/<tbody> columns, filtered to fields where show_in contains 'list' — so a field added to the schema automatically appears in the list without touching the table markup.
list_columns_usage.code: {% for field in fields %}{% if 'list' in field.show_in %}{{ field.label }}{% endif %}{% endfor %} Aksi {% for row in items %} {% for field in fields %}{% if 'list' in field.show_in %}{{ row[field.name] }}{% endif %}{% endfor %} {% endfor %}

pagination_pattern.description: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): after seeding many rows, the pagination footer was non-functional — the CRUD List template (rules/ui_templates.md section 5) had ALWAYS been static example markup (href="#", hardcoded "1"/"2"/"150") never wired to real Twig/paginator logic, and even the actual Users module built during this review only ever showed the 'Halaman X dari Y' text with no page links at all (never caught because it was only ever tested with a single seeded row). This is now a single reusable macro — write it ONCE, import it in every list view, never hand-write pagination links again. PREREQUISITE: this macro only works if canonical_snippets.eloquent_capsule_bootstrap's Paginator resolver registration is present in app/bootstrap.php — without it every page is stuck on page 1 regardless of what this macro renders. See verified_gotchas.pagination_resolvers_never_registered.

fixed_footer_macro_template.target_path: resources/views/partials/_pagination.twig — created ONCE, imported by every module's list view.

controller_must_call_appends.note: CRITICAL: the Controller MUST call ->appends($request->getQueryParams()) on the paginator BEFORE passing it to the view. Without this, clicking a page link silently drops the current ?search=... filter (and any other query params) — the paginator has no way to know what query params to preserve otherwise.

rbac_management_forms_pattern.description: The 3 admin forms every RBAC-enabled project needs: manage Roles, assign Permissions to a Role, manage Users. Role and User management are ordinary field_schema_pattern CRUD modules (worked examples below); Permission assignment is a DIFFERENT, one-off UI shape (grouped checkbox matrix) that does NOT fit the field-schema form — do not try to force it through partials/_form_field.twig.

role_field_schema_example.target_path: app/FieldSchemas/RoleFieldSchema.php — worked example of field_schema_pattern for a real module, not a new pattern.

user_field_schema_example.target_path: app/FieldSchemas/UserFieldSchema.php — note the `password` field: type=password, show_in=['add'] ONLY. It is deliberately absent from the edit form — see reset_password_admin_action below for why.
user_field_schema_example.code:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

return [
    [
        'name' => 'name',
        'label' => 'Nama Lengkap',
        'type' => 'text',
        'rules' => 'required|max:150',
        'options' => null,
        'show_in' => ['list', 'add', 'edit'],
    ],
    [
        'name' => 'username',
        'label' => 'Username',
        'type' => 'text',
        'rules' => 'required|max:100',
        'options' => null,
        'show_in' => ['list', 'add', 'edit'],
    ],
    [
        'name' => 'role_id',
        'label' => 'Role',
        'type' => 'select',
        'rules' => 'required|integer',
        'options' => null, // Controller resolves this at render time from Role::orderBy('name')->get()
        'show_in' => ['list', 'add', 'edit'],
    ],
    [
        'name' => 'password',
        'label' => 'Password',
        'type' => 'password',
        'rules' => 'required|min:8',
        'options' => null,
        'show_in' => ['add'],
    ],
];

permission_matrix_view_template.target_path: resources/views/roles/permissions.twig — a ONE-OFF page, not a reusable macro. Permissions are grouped by their `module` column (already in the permissions table since migration 0002).

permission_matrix_controller_logic.note: GET groups all permissions by module and marks which ones the role already has. POST replaces the role's permission set atomically via Eloquent's sync() — no manual diff/delete logic needed.

reset_password_admin_action.note: Why the User edit form has NO password field: an admin editing someone else's account should never see or set their literal password. Reuse the exact same random-password pattern already proven in bin/setup.php instead of inventing a new one — one button, one random password, forced change on next login.

route_wiring.note: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): a fresh project built the Role/Permission views and controller logic from this pattern, added a 'Roles' link to app/menu.php, but then FORGOT to register any /roles route in routes/web.php at all — clicking the sidebar link produced a 404. The other canonical patterns in this file (role_field_schema_example, permission_matrix_view_template, permission_matrix_controller_logic) give the Controller/View code but never the actual route registration, unlike Users which has canonical_snippets.starter_middleware_pattern.route_wiring_matching_call_sites. Add this exact block inside the same authenticated route group in routes/web.php as the /users routes (see that route_wiring_matching_call_sites for the surrounding $app->group(...)->add(new AuthMiddleware(...)) structure) — never leave a menu.php entry pointing at a route that doesn't exist.

verified_gotchas.description: Bugs that only surfaced by actually running the generated app end-to-end (login, CSRF POST, session persistence across requests) — NOT visible from reading docs or vendor source alone. Added 2026-08-06 after the first full boilerplate run. Treat every one of these as MANDATORY, not optional advice — the app is broken without them.
verified_gotchas.twig_middleware_wiring: Slim\Views\TwigMiddleware::createFromContainer($app) resolves the Twig instance via the container but NEVER sets the 'view' request attribute (its internal $attributeName stays null) — Twig::fromRequest() then always throws RuntimeException. Use TwigMiddleware::create($app, $twigInstance, 'view') instead.
verified_gotchas.middleware_add_order_includes_twig: index_php_strict_rules.middleware_execution_order must also account for TwigMiddleware: add() order is [CsrfViewMiddleware, Guard, TwigMiddleware, RoutingMiddleware (addRoutingMiddleware), BodyParsingMiddleware (addBodyParsingMiddleware), ErrorMiddleware (addErrorMiddleware)] — actual execution order (Slim is FILO: first add() = LAST to execute) is the reverse: Error -> BodyParsing -> Routing -> Twig -> Guard -> CsrfView -> handler. TwigMiddleware MUST execute before CsrfViewMiddleware, which is why it is added AFTER Guard/CsrfView even though it runs earlier.
verified_gotchas.odan_session_get_has_no_default_param: Odan\Session\SessionInterface::get(string $key) takes exactly ONE parameter — there is no `get($key, $default)` overload like Laravel/Symfony. Calling it with a second argument does not error (PHP ignores extra args) but the 'default' is silently never applied; a missing key always returns null. Use `$session->get($key) ?? $default` instead.
verified_gotchas.session_never_persisted_without_save: Odan\Session\PhpSession keeps all set()/remove()/getFlash() mutations in an in-memory ArrayObject snapshot taken at start(). It ONLY writes that snapshot back to the real $_SESSION superglobal when save() is called explicitly (save() does `$_SESSION = (array) $this->storage; session_write_close();`). If save() is never called, login appears to succeed (302 redirect) but the very next request has an empty session. Call $session->save() in the innermost middleware, right after `$handler->handle($request)` returns.
verified_gotchas.csrf_storage_conflicts_with_session_save: Slim\Csrf\Guard's default storage writes CSRF token pairs DIRECTLY into $_SESSION['csrf'] by reference, bypassing Odan's ArrayObject entirely. Once CsrfViewMiddleware calls session->save() (see above), that save() OVERWRITES $_SESSION wholesale with Odan's stale pre-Guard snapshot, deleting the token Guard just issued — every POST fails CSRF validation on the very next request. Fix: pass Guard a custom ArrayAccess+Countable+Iterator storage object that reads/writes through SessionInterface::get()/set() (see App\Support\SessionCsrfStorage in the starter boilerplate) so CSRF tokens live in the SAME tracked storage as everything else.
verified_gotchas.rakit_validation_has_no_string_rule: Rakit\Validation ships no 'string' rule at all (confirmed against vendor/rakit/validation/src/Rules — Required, Max, Min, Email, etc. exist, 'string' does not). 'required|string|max:255' throws RuleNotFoundException at runtime. Just omit it: 'required|max:255'. Only add a type rule (array/integer/numeric/boolean) when the field really is that type.
verified_gotchas.eloquent_pagination_needs_separate_packa: Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder::paginate() throws 'Class "Illuminate\Pagination\Paginator" not found' unless illuminate/pagination is required separately in composer.json — it is NOT pulled in by illuminate/database. RECURRED IN REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07) on a fresh project because this note alone wasn't enough — the AI had to infer the package name from a `use` statement instead of being given a literal composer.json to copy. Fixed properly by adding canonical_snippets.composer_json_template (the complete, verified require block, copy VERBATIM) and pointing starter_boilerplate_blueprint.json's very first directory_structure entry at it. Since app/bootstrap.php now registers Paginator resolvers on every request (see pagination_resolvers_never_registered), this package is a hard boot-time requirement from request one, not an optional add-later dependency.
verified_gotchas.no_larastan_for_standalone_eloquent: larastan/larastan (needed to make PHPStan understand Eloquent's magic __callStatic/__get) hard-crashes with 'Undefined constant Larastan\Larastan\LARAVEL_VERSION' because it requires a full illuminate/foundation Laravel Application, which this project intentionally does not have. Do NOT add larastan. Instead add targeted `ignoreErrors` regex patterns to phpstan.neon for 'Call to an undefined static method App\\Models\\...' and 'Access to an undefined property App\\Models\\...' — these are correct at runtime, PHPStan just can't see Eloquent's magic without Larastan.
verified_gotchas.field_schema_rules_must_be_filtered_by_a: VERIFIED BY ACTUALLY BUILDING A FULL CRUD MODULE (2026-08-07, Users create/edit/delete). The original field_schema_pattern design loaded ALL fields' rules into the Request's validation array regardless of action. This is wrong whenever a field's show_in excludes an action (e.g. 'password' is show_in: ['add'] only) — that field's rule ('required|min:8') would still apply on Edit even though the Edit form never renders the input, so the field is simply absent from the POST body and validation fails every time with 'password is required'. Fixed: {ModelName}Request::validate() now takes a $action ('add'|'edit') parameter and only pulls rules from fields where in_array($action, $field['show_in'], true). One shared Request class per model, not two separate {Action}{ModelName}Request classes with duplicated schema-loading logic.
verified_gotchas.middleware_constructor_call_site_mismatc: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): a local Gemini model generating a fresh project from this spec produced a fatal crash — 'RbacMiddleware::__construct(): Argument #2 ($session) must be of type Odan\Session\SessionInterface, Slim\Psr7\Factory\ResponseFactory given, called in routes/web.php on line 36'. Root cause: at the time, AuthMiddleware/RbacMiddleware/RateLimitMiddleware were listed ONLY as bare filenames in starter_boilerplate_blueprint.json with zero code — the model had to invent both the class's constructor AND its instantiation call site independently in two different files, and the parameter order/count it used for each disagreed with the other. This is the exact failure mode canonical_snippets exists to prevent, but these three classes had been missed. Fixed by adding canonical_snippets.starter_middleware_pattern with all three classes AND their exact routes/web.php call sites bundled as one inseparable unit. See also identity.rules CONSTRUCTOR_CALL_SITE_PAIRING — this class of bug can recur for ANY manually-`new`'d class, not just these three, so treat it as a standing rule, not a one-off fix.
verified_gotchas.rakit_errorbag_firstOfAll_is_keyed_by_fi: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): a local Gemini model creating a User with invalid data crashed with 'Exception::__construct(): Argument #1 ($message) must be of type string, null given' instead of showing a validation error — confirmed by directly inspecting vendor/rakit/validation/src/ErrorBag.php: firstOfAll() returns an array KEYED BY FIELD NAME (e.g. ['username' => '...', 'password' => '...']), NOT a sequential array, so `->firstOfAll()[0]` is undefined unless a field happens to be literally named '0'. This exact line (`throw new Exception($validation->errors()->firstOfAll()[0]);`) was in EVERY Request template in this spec since before the framework review even began, and had silently survived this entire session because every test exercised only successful validation or business-logic exceptions (wrong password, duplicate username) — never a genuine Rakit rule failure. FIX (applied everywhere in this spec): use `$validation->errors()->all()[0]` instead — `all()` IS a plain sequential array of messages. Lesson: a canonical_snippet is only truly verified once its FAILURE path has been exercised too, not just its happy path.
verified_gotchas.action_buttons_not_permission_gated: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): a project generated from this spec, when a user was granted only the `delete` permission for a module, still showed the 'Tambah' (Add) button in the list view even though that user has no `create` permission and clicking it would just hit a 403 from RbacMiddleware. Root cause: the original CRUD List template (rules/ui_templates.md section 5) never wrapped the Add button or the per-row Edit/Delete icons in `{% if can(...) %}` — only the ACTUAL Users module built during this review had them added, ad hoc, and that fix was never propagated back to the generic template the AI actually reads. Route-level RBAC (RbacMiddleware) and view-level RBAC (`can()` hiding the control) are BOTH required — one blocks the request, the other prevents showing a button the user isn't allowed to use in the first place.
verified_gotchas.app_shell_not_responsive: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): the navbar/sidebar App Shell did not adapt at all when the browser was resized to phone width — no hamburger button, sidebar had no responsive classes, so on a narrow screen the sidebar either overflowed off-screen or squeezed the layout instead of collapsing into a drawer. Root cause: base.twig/navbar.twig/sidebar.twig in this spec never had any responsive (mobile-drawer) markup, despite design_system naming Flowbite Admin Dashboard as the structural reference, which DOES have this pattern — it was simply never carried over. Fixed: sidebar.twig's <aside id="sidebar"> now starts off-screen on mobile (-translate-x-full) and static on desktop (lg:static lg:translate-x-0); navbar.twig has a #sidebar-toggle hamburger button (lg:hidden); base.twig has a #sidebar-backdrop overlay (lg:hidden). All three ids are wired together by initSidebarToggle() in the pre-provisioned public/assets/vendor/js/app.js — no new JS needs to be written, just include the three elements with matching ids.
verified_gotchas.pagination_footer_was_never_functional: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07): after seeding many rows into a real CRUD module ("Barang"), the pagination footer showed a single non-functional 'Berikutnya' button and no page numbers or 'Sebelumnya'. Root cause: rules/ui_templates.md section 5's pagination footer had ALWAYS been static illustrative markup (href="#", hardcoded '1'/'2'/'150') — it was never real Twig code driven by the Illuminate paginator. This spec's own reference implementation (the Users module built earlier in this review) had the SAME gap: it only ever printed 'Halaman X dari Y (Z Record)' text with zero page links, because it was only ever tested with a single seeded row and multi-page pagination was never actually exercised. Fixed with canonical_snippets.pagination_pattern — one reusable macro (partials/_pagination.twig) using the paginator's real currentPage()/lastPage()/url()/previousPageUrl()/nextPageUrl()/onFirstPage()/hasMorePages() methods, imported by every list view. Also requires the Controller to call ->appends($request->getQueryParams()) or page links silently drop the active search filter.
verified_gotchas.pagination_resolvers_never_registered: DEEPER ROOT CAUSE behind pagination_footer_was_never_functional, found by reading vendor/illuminate/pagination/AbstractPaginator.php directly (not by testing alone — the broken markup masked this second bug). illuminate/pagination used standalone (outside full Laravel, which is how this whole project uses it) does NOT auto-detect the current page or request path — Paginator::resolveCurrentPage() hardcodes a default of page 1 and resolveCurrentPath() hardcodes '/' UNLESS Paginator::currentPageResolver()/currentPathResolver()/queryStringResolver() are registered once at boot. Confirmed Eloquent\Builder::paginate() (vendor/illuminate/database/Eloquent/Builder.php:921,935) DOES call these resolvers internally, so registering them is sufficient — no other wiring needed. Without this fix, even a perfect pagination_pattern macro would have been permanently stuck on page 1 with every link pointing at '/', no matter how correct the Twig was. Fixed by adding the three resolver registrations to canonical_snippets.eloquent_capsule_bootstrap (app/bootstrap.php) — this is genuinely part of Eloquent bootstrap, not a view concern, which is why it lives there and not in pagination_pattern.
verified_gotchas.navbar_covered_by_mobile_sidebar: REPORTED DIRECTLY BY USER (2026-08-07): navbar disappeared after shrinking the browser window to phone width, and did NOT come back even after maximizing the window again. Root cause: the mobile sidebar drawer fix (app_shell_not_responsive) originally used `inset-y-0` (spans the full viewport height, top:0 to bottom:0) on a `fixed` element with `z-30`. This project's navbar (partials/navbar.twig) is NOT fixed — it is a normal-flow flex item at the top of base.twig's `flex flex-col` container. Since `fixed` positioning ignores document flow, a sidebar with `inset-y-0` starts at the very top of the VIEWPORT, overlapping the navbar's screen position, and with z-30 > navbar's z-10 it visually covers the navbar whenever the drawer is open. Resizing back to desktop width should normally restore it via `lg:static` reverting the sidebar to normal flow — if it didn't, that strongly suggests the generated code diverged from this exact class list (another instance of copy-the-literal-template mattering, not just the general shape of it). FIXED: sidebar now uses `top-16 lg:top-auto bottom-0 lg:bottom-auto` instead of `inset-y-0` — it starts exactly at the navbar's bottom edge (h-16) on mobile, so it can never visually overlap the navbar regardless of open/closed state or toggle bugs.

execution_pipeline.description: 10-Step Mandatory File Generation Contract for every feature/CRUD request

steps.name: rbac_permission_seeder
requirements: insert_permissions_with_dot_slug: '{module}.{action}' e.g. 'products.view', 'products.create' — matches the seeded core permissions (users.view, roles.view, etc.) and what canonical_snippets.rbac_management_forms_pattern's permission matrix groups by (the `module` column)

steps.name: eloquent_model
requirements: ALSO_CREATE_AND_KEEP_IN_SYNC: app/FieldSchemas/{ModelName}FieldSchema.php — single source of truth for fields, feeds steps 4 and 9. See canonical_snippets.field_schema_pattern.field_schema_template. Unlike Hooks, this file IS meant to be edited again whenever a field is added/removed/renamed.

steps.name: form_requests
steps.target_path_pattern: For CRUD modules WITH a FieldSchema: app/Requests/{ModelName}Request.php (ONE class for both Add and Edit, see canonical_snippets.field_schema_pattern.request_deriving_rules_from_schema). For standalone one-off actions with no schema (e.g. LoginRequest, ChangePasswordRequest): app/Requests/{Action}{ModelName}Request.php with hardcoded rules, same as before.
requirements: DERIVE_RULES_FROM_FIELD_SCHEMA (CRUD modules only): do NOT hardcode the rules array — load it from app/FieldSchemas/{ModelName}FieldSchema.php, filtered by $action against each field's show_in, so validation can never drift out of sync with the form/list AND never wrongly requires a field the current action's form doesn't even render. See canonical_snippets.field_schema_pattern.request_deriving_rules_from_schema.

NO_STRING_RULE: Rakit\Validation has NO 'string' rule (verified against vendor/rakit/validation/src/Rules — confirmed missing by actually running the app, see project_brain_protocol.known_issues_log pattern). NEVER write 'required|string|max:255'. A plain text field only needs 'required|max:255'; only add a type rule (array/integer/numeric/boolean) when the field really is that type.
steps.template:
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);
namespace App\Requests;

use Rakit\Validation\Validator;
use Exception;

class {ModelName}Request
{
    public static function validate(array $data, string $action): array
    {
        $fields = require dirname(__DIR__) . '/FieldSchemas/{ModelName}FieldSchema.php';

        $rules = [];
        foreach ($fields as $field) {
            if (in_array($action, $field['show_in'], true)) {
                $rules[$field['name']] = $field['rules'];
            }
        }

        $validator = new Validator();
        $validation = $validator->make($data, $rules);
        $validation->validate();
        if ($validation->fails()) {
            throw new Exception($validation->errors()->all()[0]);
        }
        return $validation->getValidData();
    }
}

steps.name: service_layer
requirements: ALSO_ENSURE_EXISTS (do not overwrite if present): app/Hooks/{ModelName}Hooks.php — see canonical_snippets.hooks_pattern.hooks_class_template and hook_protocol

steps.name: controller_layer
requirements: PAGINATOR_MUST_CALL_APPENDS: any index()/list method using ->paginate() MUST call ->appends($request->getQueryParams()) on the result before passing it to the view, or pagination links silently drop the current search/filter query params. See canonical_snippets.pagination_pattern.controller_must_call_appends.

steps.name: view_templates
requirements: USE_FIELD_SCHEMA_FOR_LIST_AND_ADD_EDIT: list table columns and add/edit form inputs MUST be generated by looping app/FieldSchemas/{ModelName}FieldSchema.php through partials/_form_field.twig (add/edit) and a plain {% for field in fields %} loop (list columns) — see canonical_snippets.field_schema_pattern.add_edit_view_usage and list_columns_usage. NEVER hand-write an <input> or <td> for a field the schema already describes.

WRAP_ACTION_BUTTONS_WITH_CAN: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07) — the 'Tambah {{ entity_name }}' button and the Edit/Delete action icons per row MUST be wrapped in `{% if can('{module}.create') %}` / `{% if can('{module}.edit') %}` / `{% if can('{module}.delete') %}` respectively. RbacMiddleware on the route only blocks direct URL access to that action — it does NOT hide the button itself, so a user with e.g. only `{module}.delete` would otherwise still see (and be confused by) an Add button they cannot use. See rules/ui_templates.md section 5 and verified_gotchas.action_buttons_not_permission_gated.

USE_PAGINATION_PARTIAL: VERIFIED BY REAL 7B TESTING (2026-08-07) — list views MUST render their pagination footer via `{% import 'partials/_pagination.twig' as pagination %}` + `{{ pagination.render(items) }}`. NEVER hand-write pagination links (href="#" or hardcoded page numbers) — that was the OLD example markup and produces a non-functional footer once there is more than one page. See canonical_snippets.pagination_pattern.
steps.template_instructions: Always include `<input type="hidden" name="{{ csrf.keys.name }}" value="{{ csrf.name }}">` and `<input type="hidden" name="{{ csrf.keys.value }}" value="{{ csrf.value }}">` in all POST forms. Delete actions MUST use the `js-confirm-delete` form class (handled by public/assets/vendor/js/app.js via SweetAlert2) instead of native `onsubmit="confirm(...)"`. base.twig MUST also render `<meta name="csrf-name" content="{{ csrf.name }}">` and `<meta name="csrf-value" content="{{ csrf.value }}">` in <head>, plus a `<div id="app-loader" class="hidden fixed inset-0 z-50 ...">` element — both are read by app.js for the Axios CSRF header and the global loading overlay.

steps.name: sidebar_navigation
requirements: APPEND_ONE_ENTRY_ONLY (see canonical_snippets.menu_registry_pattern.menu_php_template): id, label, route, icon, permission, parent

NEVER_HAND_EDIT_SIDEBAR_TWIG: resources/views/partials/sidebar.twig is a generic renderer over app/menu.php and must never be edited to add a nav link — if it needs a NEW icon key, add it to the `icons` map at the top of sidebar.twig, nothing else in that file changes

permission_filtering_is_automatic: App\Support\MenuBuilder already filters by session permissions; do not wrap menu.php entries in {% if can(...) %} — that was the OLD per-module hand-edit pattern, now obsolete

owasp_top_ten_compliance.A01_Broken_Access_Control: Enforce RBAC middleware + Data Scope validation in Service layer. Deny access by default.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A02_Cryptographic_Failures: Use password_hash(PASSWORD_BCRYPT) and bin2hex(random_bytes(32)). Mask sensitive log data.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A03_Injection: 100% Parameterized queries via Eloquent ORM. Twig auto-escaping. Ban exec() and system().
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A04_Insecure_Design: Strict 5-Layer isolation, DB::transaction auto-rollback, anti double-submit loaders.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A05_Security_Misconfiguration: Zero hardcoded credentials (.env only). Mask stack traces in production. HttpOnly/Secure cookies.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A06_Vulnerable_Components: Strict NO-CDN Policy. Serve all JS/CSS/Fonts locally from /assets/vendor/. HALT AND FATAL ERROR IF AI PUTS <link href="https://cdn..."> OR <script src="https://..."> IN TWIG FILES.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A07_Authentication_Failures: Call $session->regenerateId() via Odan\Session\SessionInterface on login. Generic auth errors ('Email/password salah'). DO NOT use raw $_SESSION.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A08_Integrity_Failures: Mandatory CSRF validation on mutating HTTP methods (provided globally by slim/csrf). Validate file upload MIME and rename files.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A09_Logging_Failures: Mandatory AuditService calls for CUD operations and security events to var/log/app.log.
owasp_top_ten_compliance.A10_SSRF: Strictly whitelist external HTTP domains if making outbound API calls.

database_transactions.pattern: Wrap multi-table CUD operations in DB::transaction(function() { ... }) for automatic rollback on failure.

centralized_error_handling.pattern: Catch exceptions centrally. Show full trace in APP_ENV=local, hide DB trace and log secretly in APP_ENV=production.

rate_limiting_and_session_expiry.pattern: Throttle login endpoints to max 5 failed attempts/15 mins per IP. Destroy session after 30 mins idle.

env_boot_validation.pattern: Verify required .env keys (APP_KEY, DB_HOST, DB_DATABASE) on application startup.

static_analysis.pattern: Code must pass PHPStan Level 5 analysis with 0 errors before deployment.

automated_testing.pattern: Generate feature/unit test in tests/Feature/{ModelName}Test.php for every new Service created.

project_brain_protocol.on_init: AI must inspect project directory and auto-generate PROJECT_BRAIN.json using the exact schema in 'schema_example' below. NEVER invent a different structure — a small model that reinvents the schema each session breaks continuity.
project_brain_protocol.on_task_complete: AI MUST update 'current_state' (last_feature, last_migration) and 'known_issues_log' in PROJECT_BRAIN.json.
